turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Walk me through a project you shipped end to end — what was the architecture and what would you change now?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I built a RAG FAQ bot for my university's CS club — FastAPI backend, Chroma for the vector store, and a Next.js frontend. The main thing I'd change is I hardcoded a 500-token chunk size with no overlap, and I only found the problem because two adjacent chunks split a definition mid-sentence and retrieval kept missing it. If I redid it I'd use a 100-token overlap and probably re-chunk by markdown headers instead of a fixed window.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: This role needs solid RAG fundamentals — how do you decide on a chunking strategy and how do you know your retrieval is actually good?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: For chunking I start from the failure mode, not a default number — if answers usually live in one paragraph, a 300-500 token chunk with 15-20% overlap works, but for code or tables I chunk by structural boundary instead. For retrieval quality I built a tiny eval set of 25 real questions with the paragraph that should be retrieved labeled, and measured recall@3 — it was 68% before I added overlap, 84% after, which is why I know the fix actually worked and wasn't just a guess.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: In your rag-faq-bot repo, chunking.py splits documents with a fixed 500-token window and no overlap. Walk me through why you picked that and what breaks with it.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: 500 tokens because that's roughly one to two paragraphs of our source docs and fit comfortably under the embedding model's context limit with room for the query. What breaks: definitions and multi-step instructions that span a chunk boundary get cut, so retrieval returns a chunk that references something explained in the previous chunk. That's the exact bug I mentioned earlier with overlap — line 34 in chunking.py is literally where I add the sliding window now.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Your llm_client.py has a retry loop that catches JSONDecodeError and retries once with a stricter prompt. Walk me through that commit and why you built it that way.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: That came from a real incident — about 1 in 20 calls the model would wrap its JSON in a markdown fence or add a one-line preamble, and json.loads would throw. I catch JSONDecodeError specifically, strip code fences, and if it still fails I retry once with an explicit 'output ONLY raw JSON' reminder appended to the prompt — capped at one retry because in testing a second retry almost never fixed it and just added latency, so past that I'd rather fail loud than silently loop.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Your README says the bot 'handles multi-turn conversations' but I don't see conversation state anywhere in the repo — can you show me where that lives?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Honestly, that line in the README is aspirational, not true yet — that's a real gap. Right now every query is stateless, I just pass the last message with no history. I got as far as sketching a Redis-backed session store keyed by a client-side session id but never wired it in before the deadline, so I'd flag that as a known limitation rather than let it slide.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Say a teammate reports the bot is suddenly returning irrelevant answers in production — walk me through how you'd debug that.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: First I'd check if it's a retrieval problem or a generation problem — pull the actual retrieved chunks for a few failing queries and read them myself. If retrieval looks fine but the answer is still bad, it's a prompt or model issue. If retrieval is bad, I'd check whether the source docs changed recently, whether the embedding model version changed, or whether the vector index just needs a re-sync. I'd also check the P95 latency graph — a sudden latency spike sometimes means we're silently falling back to a smaller/cheaper model.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's everything I had. Do you have any questions for me about the role or team?
